detail.longDescription: arXiv:2604.18585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated code generation can systematically exceed expert hand-optimization for recurrence relations--computational primitives ubiquitous in orthogonal polynomials, special functions, numerical integration, and molecular integral evaluation. We present RECURSUM, a Python DSL generating optimized C++ for arbitrary recurrence relations via three backends--template metaprogramming, a novel LayeredCodegen backend, and runtime loop-based evaluation--specifying recurrences in 10--30 lines of Python that generate 650+ lines of production C++. LayeredCodegen achieves 9.8$\times$ speedup over expert hand-written code and 1.9$\times$ over template metaprogramming for McMurchie-Davidson Hermite coefficients, through zero-copy output parameters, guaranteed inlining, and exact-sized stack buffers. A DAG-topological generalization of this architecture--built to express the four-center electron-repulsion integral that LayeredCodegen's tower model cannot--beats libint2, a mature, two-decade-refined production library, on 12 of 14 Cartesian integral classes, with $\sim$2$\times$ faster contracted Coulomb/exchange (J/K) matrix construction (alkanes and 3-D DNA fragments alike) and 1.1--2.7$\times$ faster one-electron integrals, completing the full Hartree-Fock integral set from one DAG framework. We validate 24 recurrence types spanning pure mathematics, numerical analysis, and quantum chemistry; production benchmarks confirm these speedups propagate to complete algorithms, matching expert baselines within 3.3\%. By eliminating the dual expertise barrier of domain knowledge and C++ metaprogramming, RECURSUM establishes systematic code generation--not hand-tuning--as the performance ceiling for recurrence algorithms.
